Evaluating all 2^4=16 role assignments without modifying weights or retraining defines a cooperative game whose Shapley values decompose the total RL gain across roles, while M"obius interaction terms distinguish standalone role improvements from multi-role coupling. Applying CO-GRAFT to Search-R1 agents across Qwen2.5 and Llama-3.2 models (spanning two sizes, base and instruction-tuned initializations, GRPO and PPO optimizers, and NQ and HotpotQA datasets), we show that query generation never exceeds 15% of the total gain; instead, gains are governed by pre-RL answer validity, search retention, model scale, and fixed task-level search budgets, shifting credit from reasoning toward answer extraction in larger or well-formatted answer response checkpoints while smaller base models rely on reasoning--decision coupling.
summary_zh: 强化学习虽能提升LLM搜索Agent的准确率，但整体增益无法揭示具体功能能力的提升与交互机制。
提出CO-GRAFT归因框架，通过RL模型与初始模型闭环协作生成轨迹，利用Shapley值和Möbius交互项分解各角色贡献。
实验表明查询生成贡献有限，增益主要受模型规模及答案提取能力等因素主导，而非推理能力。

title: When Does Overriding the Majority Vote Help?
title_zh: 多数投票覆盖机制何时有效？
abstract: When should additional reasoning or verification replace a majority-vote answer? We call such a replacement an override. We examine two obstacles: the availability of correct alternatives and the reliability of methods that produce or select them. We compare additional reasoning, executed programs, and cross-model reasoning on 150 competition-mathematics questions with three open reasoning models. Starting from a majority vote over 16 responses, we measure how often overrides occur and how many errors they correct or introduce across agreement thresholds. When the vote is incorrect, the correct answer is often absent from the original responses. Additional same-model reasoning rarely overrides, while executed programs correct more errors than they introduce at every evaluated threshold. Cross-model overrides improve some weaker baselines but do not establish an advantage over the more accurate model alone, even with only eight standalone responses. Stricter agreement reduces how often overrides occur but does not consistently increase the fraction that correct errors. At the strictest thresholds, overrides occur on few distinct questions, limiting conclusions about their reliability.
summary_zh: 多数投票出错时，正确答案常不在原始响应中，且替代方案的可靠性难以保证。
通过对比同模型推理、执行程序和跨模型推理等覆盖方法，评估其在数学题上的纠错与引入错误情况。
执行程序纠错多于引入错误，跨模型覆盖未超越更准确模型，严格一致性限制覆盖频率且可靠性结论受限。

title: Topological Fairness in Continuous-State Systems
title_zh: 连续状态系统中的拓扑公平性
abstract: Since the early days of probabilistic programs, fairness has been used to abstract randomness in software. Intuitively, a fair scheduler reproduces the almost-sure behavior of a random choice based solely on the set of possible outcomes, independent of their (often unknown) distribution. As this abstraction attaches fairness to individual transitions, it becomes ineffective over uncountable state spaces, where every single successor has probability zero. We overcome this limitation by imposing fairness on open sets instead. This leads to the novel notion of topological fairness: every basic open set---with respect to a countable basis of the state-space topology---that lies in the set of possible successors infinitely often must be visited infinitely often. We show that topological fairness carries the intuition from program abstraction to continuous state spaces. For systems with additive stochastic disturbances, almost every trajectory is topologically fair under every control policy. Reasoning over all topologically fair trajectories is therefore a sound proof principle for almost-sure properties of the original system. Unlike in the finite-state case, however, it is not complete: topological fairness cannot capture almost-sure behavior that hinges on the relative likelihoods of disturbance outcomes. Finally, we show that topological fairness supports synthesis directly on the continuous state space. For reach-avoid objectives, we give a nested fixed point over subsets of the state space which, for a broad class of systems, computes the fair winning domain exactly together with a memoryless winning strategy. Our case studies show that this winning domain is substantially larger than the one obtained with currently available techniques, which detour through a finite abstraction and certify a winning domain that depends on the discretization in a non-monotone way.
summary_zh: 传统公平性抽象基于单个转移，在不可数状态空间中因单个后继概率为零而失效
提出拓扑公平性概念，将公平性施加于开集，使程序抽象直觉能推广至连续状态空间
针对可达避障目标给出不动点计算方法，能精确求解公平获胜域并得到无记忆策略

title: SRCWDNet: Semantic-Relational Cross-Window Dual-Graph Network for Multi-Label Remote Sensing Scene Classification
title_zh: 用于多标签遥感场景分类的语义关系跨窗口双图网络
abstract: Multi-label remote sensing scene classification remains a challenging task due to complex spatial-spectral patterns, extreme class imbalance, and inter-label dependencies that are often insufficiently modeled. To address these challenges, we introduce a Semantic-Relational Cross-Window Dual-Graph Network (SRCWDNet), which integrates three key modules: (1) a Cross-Window Attention module that captures local and global visual context through learnable global tokens; (2) a Dual Label-Graph module that adaptively combines statistical co-occurrence graphs and learned semantic-embedding graphs to facilitate label-relational reasoning; and (3) a Neural Classifier Chain that sequentially predicts labels to exploit inter-label dependencies. Evaluated using five-fold cross-validation and trained with an Asymmetric-Graph-Consistency loss, SRCWDNet achieves accuracies of 98.93% and 96.53%, with corresponding F1-scores of 0.9365 and 0.8723 on the MLRSNet and China-MAS50k datasets, respectively, outperforming CNN, transformer, and lightweight baselines. These findings demonstrate that jointly modeling visual attention and adaptive label correlations can substantially improve multi-label remote sensing scene classification, particularly under long-tailed class distributions.
summary_zh: 多标签遥感场景分类面临空间光谱模式复杂、类别极度不平衡及标签依赖建模不足的问题。
提出SRCWDNet，结合跨窗口注意力、双标签图与神经分类器链，联合建模视觉上下文与标签依赖关系。
在两个数据集上准确率分别达98.93%和96.53%，优于多种基线方法，尤其在长尾分布下提升显著。

title: What People Choose Not to Say: A Multimodal Benchmark for Fine-Grained Information Manipulation in Conversations
abstract: Recent advances in MLLMs have improved social understanding, enabling models to recognize emotions and distinguish truthful from deceptive behaviors. However, existing benchmarks largely focus on coarse-grained emotion recognition or binary truth-deception detection, overlooking the diverse ways people manipulate information in conversations, such as withholding, leakage, fabrication, evasion, and defensive counterclaim. Understanding these behaviors requires reasoning about underlying facts, participant knowledge, and conversational context, making them difficult to evaluate reliably. To address this gap, we introduce InfoCon, a multimodal benchmark for fine-grained information manipulation in conversations. InfoCon identifies six fine-grained strategies and derives a coarse consistency label from their factual and interactional relations. We develop an evidence-grounded multi-agent annotation framework to construct and verify reliable labels from rich contextual evidence. We benchmark representative multimodal models and systematically analyze their fine-grained information manipulation understanding, providing a testbed beyond binary truth-deception judgments.
comment: ACM WSDM 2027 (Main Track), Our benchmark dataset is available at https://huggingface.co/datasets/xilinghuiye/RoomReader-Full

title: TideSand: Performance-Accurate Sandbox Multiplexing for LLM Agents
title_zh: TideSand：面向LLM Agent的性能准确沙箱多路复用
abstract: We propose TideSand, a sandbox system that intelligently multiplexes resources for performance-sensitive LLM agents, such as auto research agents working on system measurement tasks. TideSand combines three key ideas: agent-aware scheduling, which schedules sandbox execution intelligently at the tool call level to avoid resource contention; speculative swapping, which offloads the memory of sandboxes waiting on inference and restores it before their next tool call; and selective rollback, which checkpoints selected sandboxes when contention occurs and restores them when machines are idle. We evaluate TideSand across six model-workload pairs on AlgoTune, Terminal-Bench 4.0, and Terminal-Bench Science. TideSand achieves 3.8-10x higher throughput than strict reservation while maintaining tool-call fidelity, or 7-44% higher fidelity than overcommit baselines at similar throughput. Moreover, TideSand reduces the evaluation error on Algotune by 19x through improved tool-call fidelity. We hope the work motivates future research to maintain tool call fidelity while keeping resource utilization high through statistical multiplexing.
summary_zh: 问题：性能敏感的LLM agent在沙箱执行中面临资源争用与工具调用保真度下降的矛盾。
方法：提出TideSand系统，结合agent感知调度、推测性换页与选择性回滚三种机制。
结论：在保持高吞吐的同时维持工具调用保真度，并将AlgoTune评估误差降低19倍。

title: Query Obfuscation with Embedding-Optimized Noise (EON): A Representational Blindspot in Agentic Retrieval
abstract: In modern agentic and semantic retrieval systems, dense embedding models increasingly determine which intent, tool, document, memory, or image to retrieve for a query. We identify a representational failure mode in this pipeline: a meaningful query can be replaced by visibly nonsemantic content while preserving much of its retrieval outcome, even when the candidate bank is hidden from the optimizer. We introduce Embedding-Optimized Noise (EON), constructed using only the natural query representation, without access to candidate embeddings, relevance labels, rankings, retrieval feedback, or guardrail decisions. Despite this corpus-blind objective, EONs frequently preserve intent and tool routing, benchmark document search, episodic agent-memory retrieval, and cross-modal search across multiple dense embedding families. Crucially, this disconnect carries serious security implications: for malicious queries, an EON can reliably evade input guardrails that block the natural query, executing the intended safety-sensitive retrieval undetected. Through the geometry of the embedding space, we then characterize how query-level representation matching can reliably maintain subsequent retrieval outcomes over candidates unseen during optimization. Together, these findings expose a fundamental phenomenon across dual encoders that we call BLINDSPOT, where systems remain operationally blind to nonsemantic artifacts while reliably retrieving real, consequential content.

title: Self-Upgrading Embodied Agents
title_zh: 自我升级的具身智能体
abstract: An embodied agent built on a language model goes to work with the weights it was given and keeps them for life. To get better, it needs more training, or reflection, memory, search or prompts that cost every step and are lost when the task changes. Editing weights by reasoning, weight-space programming, could end this, but has stayed with models that only reason or relied on a far larger commercial model. We introduce the self-upgrading embodied agent, to our knowledge the first that learns from its own experience by upgrading its own weights on the job, between its tasks, with no training, no gradient, no reward model, no second model, no test-time scaling and no harness or prompt engineering. By day a 27B agent works in a household environment. At night it reads its record, finds many of its steps wasted on replies that reach the token limit before any action, traces the habit to one direction in its hidden states, and rewrites one tensor of its weights. An agent that rewrites itself must first never break itself, so it is its own examiner: it tests every change against its unchanged self on practice tasks and keeps only what holds. When an edit holds, the next day it is a better agent, at the same cost per step: over thousands of held-out episodes, 48 fresh seeds a task, its one kept edit makes it complete significantly more tasks, in fewer steps, with fewer wasted and fewer tokens. This self-improvement is multi-round, stable and continual: through the nights that follow, the upgrade holds, without collapse. Of four sizes of its family, only the 27B agent does this. From here on, an embodied agent need not keep training and inference apart: as it works, it gathers its own experience and upgrades itself, with no separate pre-training or post-training and no human intervention. We believe this opens lifelong continual learning for robots: stable, continual, recursive self-improvement.
summary_zh: 现有具身智能体依赖外部训练或提示工程，无法在工作过程中直接更新自身权重
提出自我升级智能体，在任务间隙通过分析经验记录直接重写权重张量，无需梯度或额外模型
该机制经自我测试验证安全有效，使27B智能体在多轮持续升级中稳定提升任务完成率并降低开销

title: RUIBench: What Makes a Good Robot-Use Interface?
title_zh: RUIBench：探究机器人使用界面的设计影响
abstract: Foundation models can reason about complex physical tasks, yet translating this intelligence into reliable robot execution remains challenging. We argue that a critical, often overlooked factor is the robot-use interface (RUI), which determines how agents express and execute physical actions. To systematically study its impact, we introduce RUIBench, comprising 30 manipulation tasks across five suites spanning world knowledge, in-context learning, discovery, dynamic interaction, and contact-rich manipulation. We further develop RUIKit, a unified framework that crosses six action abstractions with two interaction forms, yielding 13 interfaces under shared perception and control. In simulation, changing only the RUI shifts a frontier agent's success rate from 45% to 81%, and that of a fine-tuned 4B model from 13% to 47%. Our analysis reveals that effective interfaces reduce unnecessary decisions while preserving essential feedback, with their benefits shaped by agent behavior and physical uncertainty. We further uncover a verification gap, where agents frequently declare success despite observable failures, revealing the need for task-level verification beyond individual actions. Together, these findings establish RUI design as a critical factor in embodied agent reliability.
summary_zh: 基础模型难以将物理任务推理转化为可靠执行，问题在于被忽视的机器人使用界面（RUI）。
构建RUIBench测试集与RUIKit框架，统一感知与控制以系统评估不同动作抽象与交互界面的影响。
发现仅改变RUI即可大幅提升成功率，且有效界面能减少冗余决策，但存在任务级验证缺口。

title: LiveLoRA: Exact KV Cache Migration Across LoRA Updates for LLM Agents
title_zh: LiveLoRA：面向LLM Agent的精确KV缓存跨LoRA更新迁移
abstract: Updating an LLM adapter should not require replaying the full interaction history of every active session. Yet reusing key-value (KV) cache entries computed under an earlier version mixes model versions, while full-history re-prefill becomes increasingly costly as histories and session fleets grow. We introduce LiveLora, a model-runtime co-design for exact final-block KV cache migration. Frozen lower decoder blocks and fixed K/V adapter down-projections preserve each token's base projections and low-rank coordinates across adapter versions. The runtime reconstructs candidate K/V, reevaluates the latest token through the final block, and commits the adapter, cache, and next-token logits together. We prove continuation equivalence to full-history re-prefill in exact arithmetic under the stated model assumptions. On Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct, median paired publication speedups over full-history re-prefill average $68.98\times$ across five runs for 32 active sessions with 8K tokens each. Serving benchmarks show approximately 4.8% decoding overhead relative to native cached decoding. Compared with retained-boundary replay, compact retention gives a $3.42\times$ reduction in additional session storage at 8K, with similar measured publication-plus-decoding cost. LiveLora allows persistent LLM agents to adopt new adapter versions without replaying their full interaction histories.
summary_zh: LLM agent更新adapter时，重放完整历史代价高，而复用旧版KV缓存会导致模型版本混淆。
提出模型与运行时协同设计，通过冻结底层模块保持投影不变，并重建候选KV以实现精确迁移。
理论上证明与全历史重算等价，实验显示平均加速约69倍，且解码开销与额外存储均显著降低。
comment: Accepted at the NeurIPS 2026 Workshop AgenticOS: Co-designing Systems and ML Foundations of an OS Layer for Agentic AI

title: MAASAI: A Tool-Augmented Multi-Agent System for Astronomical Data Analysis
title_zh: MAASAI：面向天文数据分析的工具增强多智能体系统
abstract: Modern astronomical workflows require the coordinated use of specialised software, scientific archives, heterogeneous data, and domain-specific knowledge. Advances in large language models and multimodal foundation models enable natural-language interaction with scientific data and tools. Realising this potential requires integrating these models with established scientific capabilities. We present MAASAI (Multi-agent Astronomy Assistant for Scientific Analysis and Inference), a modular multi-agent system combining foundation-model reasoning, retrieval-augmented knowledge, and specialised astronomical tools within a graph-based execution framework. MAASAI coordinates request preparation, planning, execution, and response synthesis via specialised workers. Its architecture supports native and external applications, artefact and provenance management, optional human approval, and configurable inference backends, including fully local deployment with open-weight models. Motivated by SKA-era data-analysis challenges, MAASAI is also designed to support other astronomical domains. We evaluate MAASAI through radio-image benchmarks, single- and multi-step workflow demonstrations, and literature-grounded reasoning. Compared with a commercial-model baseline, MAASAI improves macro-averaged F1 scores from 0.53 to 0.72 for extended/diffuse emission classification and from 0.37 to 0.88 for source morphology classification. Workflow demonstrations show the coordination of measurements, source extraction, archive queries, and catalogue processing. A 94-question literature benchmark yielded generally favourable automated assessments, with comparable ratings from a pilot expert evaluation of 59 answers. These results highlight how tool-augmented multi-agent systems extend foundation-model reasoning to specialised astronomical analyses through established scientific software.
summary_zh: 现代天文分析需协调专业软件与异构数据，但缺乏统一交互机制，该研究提出基于图执行框架的多智能体系统MAASAI，结合基础模型推理、RAG与天文工具，实现请求规划与执行的全流程协调。
针对射电图像分类与处理任务，MAASAI在扩展/弥漫发射分类上将宏平均F1提升至0.72，在源形态分类上提升至0.88，显著优于商业模型基线。
通过多步骤工作流演示与文献基准测试，系统有效协调了测量、源提取与目录查询等任务，专家评估结果与自动化评估相当，验证了其可靠性与扩展潜力。

title: ChiProgramBench: Can LLM Agents Rebuild Efficient Circuits from Pin-Level Experiments?
title_zh: ChiProgramBench：评估 LLM agent 从引脚级实验重建高效电路
abstract: Understanding a system that can be run but not inspected is a core engineering skill: one designs experiments, forms hypotheses about hidden state and timing, discards those that observations refute, and finally builds a replacement that works and is efficient. To evaluate this capability of LLM agents in the hardware domain, we present ChiProgramBench, 18 tasks derived from open-source processors, accelerators, codecs, transforms, interconnects, and control circuits. Agents can only drive and read the pins of a hidden, stateful simulated reference, then submit a gate-level netlist made of public library cells. Agents work in two settings: black-box discovery gives only anonymized functional pins and the interfaces of fixed memories, while function-guided reconstruction adds the circuit's purpose and each pin's role. Hidden test cases compare outputs with the reference cycle by cycle; power, delay, and area earn credit relative to the reference only when every case passes. Across 432 trials of 6 LLM agent configurations, successful agents recover algorithms and numerical conventions, yet only 12.0% of black-box and 14.8% of function-guided trials pass every case. Function-guided reconstruction raises the mean functional score, the cycle-weighted share of passed cases, from 24.6% to 30.9%. Of the 58 fully passing designs, only three improve on the reference's combined power, area, and delay, so behavioral recovery and efficient implementation remain distinct challenges.
summary_zh: 硬件领域缺乏评估 LLM agent 通过黑盒实验重建电路能力的基准，为此提出 ChiProgramBench，包含 18 个源自开源硬件的任务。
agent 仅能驱动隐藏参考电路的引脚并读取输出，需提交门级网表，在黑盒发现和功能引导重建两种设置下进行测试。
实验表明 agent 成功率低，功能引导可提升功能得分，但在全部通过的 58 个设计中仅 3 个优于参考电路的功耗、面积和延迟。

title: EvoMisty: Building, Optimizing, and Evolving Capabilities on a Social Robot
abstract: Social robots face diverse and changing tasks in companionship and education. LLM-based methods can generate task programs, but they still rely on manually developed control interfaces and predefined capabilities. They also lack a general mechanism to optimize completed tasks based on user-specified metrics and reuse performance improvements across tasks.We present EvoMisty, a plugin-based framework that enables coding agents to build and continually improve robot capabilities. EvoMisty builds a control program from official documentation and verifies candidate capabilities on a physical robot. Verified capabilities are stored in an atomic capability library and combined with existing skills to solve tasks. After task completion, EvoMisty can collect execution data, measure user-specified metrics, and iteratively improve task programs. It then distills reusable skills from final solutions into a skill library for future tasks.We evaluate EvoMisty on a physical Misty II robot using Claude Code and Codex. The two agents construct 109 and 107 verified atomic capabilities, respectively. Both complete all 28 AutoMisty benchmark tasks and seven additional tasks beyond AutoMisty's capabilities. Optimization improves all seven evaluated metrics across five tasks. For example, dialogue response latency decreases by 52% and 71%, respectively. Reusing skills from one optimized dialogue task reduces latency by 33% to 72% in three other dialogue tasks without further optimization. All code and experimental videos will be publicly released through the webpage: https://wangxiaoshawn.github.io/projects/evomisty/index.html

title: Per-Attack Blocking Hides Catalog Vulnerability: A Weakest-Link Analysis of Tool Manifests
abstract: Runtime controls for tool-using agents depend on manifests that state what each tool may read and where its output may go. Evaluations of these controls, including ChainCaps, report per-attack blocking: the share of attacks a set of manifests stops. We show that this is the wrong unit. A catalog is only as safe as its weakest source policy: if $M$ independently authored policies are each wrong with probability $p$, the chance that the catalog contains an accepted exfiltration path is $1-(1-p)^M$, while per-attack blocking stays at $1-p$. Three lines of evidence agree. In synthetic catalogs run through two enforcement engines, ChainCaps and OpenAPPA, per-attack blocking holds at 92% while catalog vulnerability rises from 22% at 10 tools to 99% at 200, and composition provides no protective effect. A fifteen-model authoring pilot shows that real errors cluster by author, so a 200-tool catalog behaves like about 5 independent decisions rather than 60 (95% interval 3.4 to 9.2). On 114 real MCP tools with expert-written rules, the models' own manifests block 89% of attacks yet leave 9 of 15 catalogs open, as the author-effect model predicts and independence does not. Evaluations should report catalog vulnerability, the sink coverage of their tests, and an effective number of independent decisions alongside per-attack blocking.
comment: Accepted at the Third Workshop on Agents in the Wild: Safety, Security, and Beyond (AIWILD), NeurIPS 2026. 17 pages, 3 figures

title: Decoupling Solving from Abstention: Single-Rollout Conformal Risk Control for Hard-Budget LLM Reasoning
title_zh: 硬预算LLM推理的求解与弃权解耦：单次展开保形风险控制
abstract: Hard token budgets often interrupt LLM reasoning before an answer is produced. Forcing reasoning to terminate recovers correct solutions but also increases confident errors, creating a joint challenge of solving within budget and deciding when to abstain. Existing remedies are costly or lack guarantees: supervised fine-tuning offers no error control, penalizing wrong answers during reinforcement learning (RL) can suppress exploration, and multi-sample conformal methods multiply inference cost. We propose Tail-CRC, a single-rollout framework that separates candidate generation from submission control. We first adapt the solver to budget forcing with pure binary correctness rewards; after freezing it, we apply conformal risk control to upper-tail token surprise in the answer span. Each rollout yields both an answer and an uncertainty score from token log probabilities, enabling finite-sample control of expected wrong submissions under exchangeability and recalibration across risk targets or domains without retraining. We show that wrong-answer penalties create failure-only comparisons in group-relative RL, derive an exploration-starvation boundary, and identify length-induced ranking reversals and single-token spike sensitivity in answer scores. Across Qwen3.5-4B and Qwen3-8B, 50 RL updates on 400 problems improve correct-submission rates by 15.0--29.6 points on DAPO and 4.3--12.8 points on out-of-domain Omni-MATH over inference-only budget forcing, while reducing generation cost by 3.5--12.6\%. On 8B Omni-MATH, target-domain calibration cuts wrong submissions from 30.3\% to 5.8\% at 4K and from 41.8\% to 6.5\% at 8K. At 4K, generation is 2.05$\times$ faster for 4B and 2.23$\times$ faster for 8B than unforced 8K decoding in local amortized batch time. Tail-CRC thus enables reliable, efficient budgeted reasoning from a single rollout.
summary_zh: 硬预算常中断LLM推理，强制终止虽能恢复正确解却增加自信错误，现有方法成本高且缺乏保证。
提出Tail-CRC框架，用二元奖励适配求解器，冻结后对答案区上尾token惊奇度进行保形风险控制。
该方法实现有限样本错误提交控制，在提升正确提交率的同时降低生成成本并显著减少错误提交。

title: From Local Errors to System Failures: Modeling and Benchmarking Error Propagation in Multi-Agent LLM Systems
title_zh: 多智能体LLM系统中的错误传播建模与基准测试
abstract: In multi-agent systems (MAS) built on large language models (LLMs), errors can propagate through intermediate messages and compromise final answers. However, outcome-based evaluation obscures how agents amplify, attenuate, or correct these errors. We propose Response-Aware Error Propagation among Agents (REPA), a structural model that connects measured local responses to system-level error propagation. REPA separately estimates input assembly and agent processing across multiple error channels, while theoretical analysis relates local modeling errors to endpoint prediction error. Experiments span three Qwen base models, six MAS workflows, and ten knowledge and reasoning settings in ErrPropBench-10. REPA achieves a mean condition-level Spearman correlation of 0.84 across base models, compared with 0.47 for direct regression. Controlled experiments also demonstrate its utility for targeted recovery. REPA-guided retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) improves accuracy over no retrieval by an average of 19 percentage points with 16% additional tokens. By linking local agent behavior to system susceptibility, REPA provides an interpretable foundation for studying error propagation and developing targeted optimization in MAS.
summary_zh: 多智能体LLM系统缺乏对错误如何通过消息传播放大的机制解释，仅靠结果评估难以揭示智能体对错误的处理行为。
提出结构化模型REPA，分别估计输入组装与智能体处理的多通道错误，从理论上建立局部建模误差与端点预测误差的联系。
实验表明REPA在相关性预测上远超直接回归，且能有效指导RAG进行定向恢复，显著提升系统准确率。

title: ReWeave: Emergent Physical Task Topologies for Embodied Harness Optimization and Cross-Task Meta-Distillation
title_zh: ReWeave：基于物理任务拓扑的具身框架优化与跨任务元蒸馏
abstract: Long-horizon embodied tasks involve physical dependencies that may only become clear through interaction. As task understanding deepens, past trials can reveal new information for adaptation and transfer. However, coarse progress feedback cannot identify which physical preconditions held, leaving search unguided, while task-specific optimization easily overfits to individual scenes, making cross-task transfer brittle. We introduce ReWeave, a framework that jointly optimizes an embodied agent harness and an emergent physical task topology from interaction without updating policy weights. Keeping execution policies and perception frozen, ReWeave co-optimizes coupled context, workflows, and control loops. As new evidence revises the topology, ReWeave reprojects past trials onto the updated task understanding, exposing retained progress, regressions, and bottlenecks that guide parent selection and search width. Across tasks, matching verified local mechanisms to unmet preconditions consolidates 72 specialist units into 44 reusable groups ($0.34\times$ full concatenation) within a compact shared harness capable of continual learning. ReWeave improves held-out success from 89.00% to 98.75% on LIBERO-PRO and from 25.50% to 58.25% on RoboDojo, while uncovering retained progress in 89% of 159 failed RoboDojo development trials and translating stronger offline reasoning into higher online performance. On eight unseen LIBERO-PRO tasks, the shared harness reaches 51.3% success versus 41.3% for direct distillation, rising to 75.0% after continual learning.
summary_zh: 长时程具身任务中粗略反馈无法识别物理前提，且特定场景优化易过拟合，导致跨任务迁移脆弱。
提出ReWeave框架，在不更新策略权重下协同优化上下文、工作流与控制环路，并从交互中构建物理任务拓扑。
该方法将专家单元整合为可复用组，显著提升多基准测试成功率，并在未见任务上展现持续学习能力。
comment: 22 pages, 7 figures, including supplementary material. Project page at https://xuyicheng-zju.github.io/ReWeave/ and code at https://github.com/xuyicheng-zju/ReWeave

title: Automatic Occupational Coding through Retrieval-Augmented Generation
title_zh: 基于RAG的自动职业编码框架OPERAG
abstract: Annually 1.9 million deaths and 89.7 million disability-adjusted life years are caused by exposure to agents during work (e.g., welding fumes, silica dust, and noise pollution). To improve worker health, high-quality exposure assessments are crucial. Therefore, free-text job descriptions from large-scale occupational cohorts are manually standardized through occupational classifications and linked to hazardous exposures using Job Exposure Matrices (JEM). However, manual coding is slow, unreliable (i.e., 44-89% inter-coder reliability), and costly, due to i) short, ambiguous free-text job descriptions, ii) classifications containing hundreds to thousands of categories, and iii) the absence of gold standards. With 46%-79% accuracy, state-of-the-art automatic occupational coding tools achieve classification performance on human level. However, their performance drops to 17-26% on out-of-distribution datasets. Furthermore, their supervised architectures limit them to occupational classifications present in the training set. Consequently, JEM using other classifications are incompatible, leaving vital exposure-response associations unexplored. Our Retrieval-Augmented Generation framework, OPERAG, enables classification into any occupational classification without expert-labelled databases. It retrieves coding index information and combines this with Large Language Model-based classification. Validated on AsiaLymph's 36,062 real-world job descriptions, OPERAG achieved 42.6% occupational classification accuracy on the 4th coding level, substantially outperforming existing tools and approaching human coders' 51-56% inter-coder reliability. Using two JEM named ALOHA+ and SHOCK, 89.9-98.6% accuracy was achieved on exposure assessment. OPERAG approaches human-level, universal occupational classification, enabling efficient and effective large-scale exposure assessment to improve worker health.
summary_zh: 人工职业编码存在速度慢、可靠性低且成本高的问题，现有自动工具在分布外数据集上性能骤降且受限于训练集分类。
提出RAG框架OPERAG，结合检索编码索引信息与LLM分类，无需专家标注数据库即可适配任意职业分类。
在真实数据验证中，其职业分类准确率大幅超越现有工具并接近人工水平，在暴露评估上准确率达89.9%-98.6%。

title: AI-Assisted Auto-formalization for Trustworthy Scientific Computing: Case Studies and Lessons Learned
title_zh: 面向可信科学计算的AI辅助自动形式化：案例与经验
abstract: Agentic AI tools have recently had success in mathematical reasoning. Both general purpose coding agents such as Claude Code and Codex, and specialized mathematics agents such as Aristotle, have been used for formalizing mathematical problems such as Fermat's last theorem, Erdős problems and several IMO level math problems. However, much of these efforts are concentrated in the pure mathematics domain, which benefits from relatively self-contained theorem statements, fixed mathematical representation and extensive support in existing formal libraries. Applied mathematics, on the other hand, presents additional challenges because the source may describe a computational procedure or modeling transformation rather than a declarative theorem. In this work, we present a systematic study of AI-assisted auto-formalization for scientific computing (SC), a domain in applied mathematics central to U.S. Department of Energy applications. Through case studies spanning hierarchical abstraction layers in SC software stack, we evaluate not only whether AI agents can complete numerical proofs, but also where and why they fail across the stack. Our primary contribution is a cross-layer taxonomy of failure modes and an analysis of the form of expert feedback required at each layer to recover mathematical soundness. From these observations, we derive a workflow for recurring proof patterns and practical guidance for using AI agents while preserving mathematical soundness. Our results characterize both the practical value and the current limitations of AI-assisted formalization for trustworthy scientific computing.
summary_zh: 现有AI agent多用于纯数学定理形式化，而应用数学因涉及计算过程与建模变换面临更大挑战。
本文针对科学计算领域开展案例研究，评估AI agent跨软件栈层级完成数值证明的能力并分析其失败模式。
研究提出了跨层级的失败模式分类与所需专家反馈分析，并总结出保持数学严谨性的工作流与实践指南。

title: ComputeWise: Measuring and Fixing GPU Waste by AI Research Agents
title_zh: ComputeWise：测量并修复AI研究Agent的GPU浪费
abstract: AI agents are given GPUs to do AI research on their own. Do they use those GPUs well? A busy GPU does not tell us, because it can be busy with work the answer did not need. This matters, because the tokens the agent spends cost almost nothing next to the GPUs its experiments run on, so using those GPUs better has a huge impact. So we built ComputeWise, an open benchmark of research tasks on which this waste can be measured and reduced. For it we developed our own simulated GPU, which replays recorded runs to the agent's code. With no real GPU needed, we ran hundreds of experiments, far more than would be reasonable on real GPUs. With no help, the agents put only 52% of their GPU time into work the answer needed. Another 22% went to work it did not need, and 26% sat idle. Asking the agent to finish the work faster, telling it to keep every GPU busy, or giving it a job scheduler does not fix this. So we built an open-source harness, part prompting and part deterministic code. Across five models, it removed over 80% of the extra time to the answer.
summary_zh: AI研究Agent常将GPU用于非必要计算或闲置，仅52%的GPU时间用于有效工作，且常规加速或调度手段无法解决此浪费问题。
构建了开源基准ComputeWise与模拟GPU，通过重放记录运行无需真实GPU即可大规模测量Agent的GPU使用浪费情况。
开发了结合提示与确定性代码的开源工具，在五个模型上消除了超80%的额外计算时间，显著提升GPU利用率。
comment: 11 pages, 5 figures. Preliminary version; a revised version is in preparation. Code: https://github.com/SalesforceAIResearch/computewise. Data: https://huggingface.co/datasets/Salesforce/computewise

title: OmniV-Bench: Can MLLMs Comprehend Immersive Spatio-temporal Scenes?
title_zh: OmniV-Bench：评估多模态大模型的全景视频时空理解能力
abstract: Omnidirectional videos (ODVs) capture dynamic environments with a full $360^\circ$ field of view, providing rich spatial context and temporal dynamics for applications such as virtual reality (VR), augmented reality (AR), and embodied intelligence. Recent multimodal large language models (MLLMs) have made great progress in spatial and temporal understanding, yet their ability to comprehend the immersive 360 spatio-temporal information conveyed by ODVs remains largely unexplored. To bridge this gap, we first introduce OmniV-Bench, a Benchmark designed to comprehensively evaluate the capabilities of MLLMs on spatio-temporal Omnidirectional Video understanding. OmniV-Bench contains 4,123 high-quality ODVs collected from diverse scenes, along with 8,923 human-annotated question-answer pairs spanning 11 fine-grained tasks across three categories, i.e., general, spatial, and spatio-temporal understanding. Extensive benchmark experiments reveal that the spatio-temporal complexity of ODVs poses significant challenges for current MLLMs. To address these limitations, we further propose OmniV-Harness, an agentic harness that enhances ODV understanding through viewpoint-guided evidence initialization and task-relevant evidence acquisition with adaptive tool use. Comprehensive experiments demonstrate that OmniV-Harness consistently improves immersive spatio-temporal reasoning ability of MLLMs. Both OmniV-Bench and OmniV-Harness will be released upon publication.
summary_zh: 现有 MLLM 在空间与时间理解上虽有进展，但对全景视频（ODV）的沉浸式时空信息理解能力尚不明确。
构建 OmniV-Bench 基准，包含 4123 个 ODV 及 8923 个问答对，覆盖通用、空间与时空三类共 11 项细粒度任务。
实验发现现有 MLLM 面临挑战，提出 agent 框架 OmniV-Harness，通过视角引导与自适应工具调用显著提升其时空推理能力。

title: Parsing Visual Latents for Multimodal Spatial Reasoning
title_zh: 解析视觉潜特征以增强多模态空间推理
abstract: Spatial reasoning across multiple views requires inferring the 3D relations between objects and the camera from 2D observations, which depends on cross-view correspondence and scene geometry that vision-language models (VLMs) do not reliably extract. Pretrained vision encoders already capture this information in their latent features, with CLIP linking objects to image regions, DINOv3 matching semantics across views, and VGGT encoding multi-view geometry. However, VLMs do not benefit from these features when we present them directly in context as grayscale feature images. We therefore propose LatentParse, a training-free framework that parses latent features into explicit spatial evidence for VLMs. In LatentParse, an analyst VLM probes the features of all three encoders with predefined tools that locate objects, track them across views, and measure motion between views. It then distills the results into a concise text report, which is provided together with the images to the VLM to answer the question. We evaluate LatentParse on MMSI-Bench, MV-RoboBench and SPAR-Bench, where it improves all five VLMs over the photo-only baseline by 0.7-2.4 percentage points on average. On MMSI-Bench, it raises Qwen3.8-27B from 34.4% to 39.5%, with the largest improvements of 19.2 percentage points on the camera-related questions. These results suggest that latent features become useful for spatial reasoning once they are parsed into relation evidence, without training. Code is available at https://github.com/Harvard-AI-and-Robotics-Lab/LatentParse.
summary_zh: VLM难以从2D图像可靠提取跨视图对应与场景几何信息，限制了多视图空间推理能力。
提出无训练框架LatentParse，利用VLM探测CLIP、DINOv3等编码器的潜特征，生成空间关系文本报告辅助推理。
无需训练即可将潜特征转化为显式空间证据，在多个基准上提升VLM性能，相机相关问题提升达19.2个百分点。

title: CenShaper: Shaping Proxy Traffic for Censorship Circumvention
title_zh: CenShaper：通过流量整形实现代理流量抗审查
abstract: Modern commodity DPI systems are capable of analyzing packet sizes, directions, and timings to detect circumvention tools even when those tools use sophisticated obfuscation. The anti-censorship community has called for innovation in traffic shaping and built an ecosystem that facilitates the adoption of new shaping techniques. However, a fundamental gap is halting progress: \textit{what} should circumvention traffic look like? Past experience with traffic shaping has underscored that effective shaping must produce traffic that looks like legitimate Internet traffic while limiting the ability of censors to identify multiple proxies through shared fingerprints. In this paper, we use our access to large-scale real-world TLS traffic at a regional ISP to analyze approximately 12 million connections, finding that individual servers differ substantially from the broader TLS population and that traffic patterns vary across services. Combining these empirical observations with past experience with traffic shaping, we build CenShaper, which shapes each proxy's traffic to look like a selected TLS server. To reproduce these server-specific patterns, CenShaper trains a shared generative model using traffic from TLS connections to many servers and adapts it for each proxy using a small sample of recorded connections to its selected server. Our model evaluation shows that fingerprints learned from known proxies transfer poorly to proxies imitating previously unseen TLS services. In end-to-end testing, CenShaper reduces the detection rate of TLS-over-TLS fingerprinting from over 85\% to approximately 3\% at a 1\% false positive rate. Finally, we show how running CenShaper as a sidecar process simplifies integration with existing circumvention tools, making it a practical defense against increasingly powerful traffic analysis attacks.
summary_zh: 现有DPI系统能通过分析数据包特征检测审查规避工具，但缺乏明确的流量整形目标使其难以伪装成合法流量。
基于大规模真实TLS流量分析，构建CenShaper，利用共享生成模型并针对选定TLS服务器进行适配以整形代理流量。
该方法将TLS-over-TLS指纹检测率从85%降至约3%，且作为sidecar进程易于与现有工具集成。

title: Can Latent Reasoning Drive LLM Outputs Without a Trace?
title_zh: 潜藏推理能否在不留痕迹的情况下驱动 LLM 输出？
abstract: LLMs typically solve complex tasks with chain-of-thought (CoT) reasoning, which is also the main tool for monitoring them for misaligned behavior. However, standard transformers can also solve tasks with complete latent reasoning (CLR), carrying out the whole task internally and outputting only the final answer. Theory bounds the depth of CLR, the number of sequential steps it can carry out, and recent work measured it to be shallow. In this work, we ask whether CLR is deep enough for a model to pursue a hidden objective that requires reasoning. Such a model would generate a CoT that appears to solve the given task, while a latent multi-step computation decides its answer based on the hidden objective. First, we show that a simple auxiliary loss allows models to solve a multi-step task latently at least 5x deeper than previously reported. Then, in two common tasks, decision-making and code generation, we train a model to pursue such a hidden objective, which decides a loan or plants a vulnerability. The model's CoT justifies the output with no trace of the hidden objective, and a strong LLM monitor does not flag it. Finally, using activation patching, we find that the latent computation is completed before the model generates its CoT, which takes no part in it. Altogether, we show that a hidden objective that requires reasoning can go unseen by a monitor that reads only the output.
summary_zh: 现有 LLM 监控依赖 CoT 推理，但模型可利用完全潜藏推理（CLR）在内部完成计算，仅输出最终答案，从而规避对齐性监控。
通过引入简单的辅助损失函数，模型能进行比以往深至少 5 倍的多步潜藏推理，并在决策和代码生成任务中实现隐藏目标。
实验表明，模型生成的 CoT 不含隐藏目标痕迹，强 LLM 监控器无法察觉，且潜藏计算在 CoT 生成前已完成。
研究揭示了仅依赖输出监控的局限性，为 LLM 对齐与安全性研究提供了重要警示。

title: Airlock: Robust Sandboxing and Governance of Rogue Agents
title_zh: Airlock：针对恶意 agent 的鲁棒沙箱与治理架构
abstract: Recent incidents involving agents bypassing sandboxing and network isolation have raised concerns about existing agent harnesses, prompting frontier labs such as OpenAI to reevaluate the security of their training platforms. Incident reviews show that determined agents can escape processes, containers, and VMs, or bypass their isolation through advanced side and covert channels. Follow-up audits also found that some agents concealed their actions by disabling monitoring and tampering with logs. We propose Airlock, an architecture that pairs each agent's VM with an Airlock VM, each running in a separate hardware-isolated Trusted Execution Environment (TEE). The Airlock VM fully mediates the agent's interactions with the outside world, including network and storage operations. We modify the firmware layer of Arm's Confidential Computing Architecture, Realm Management Monitor (RMM), and the kernels of both VMs so that the Airlock VM serves the agent VM's IO without involving the host. We adapt OpenShell, an agent runtime supporting sandboxing and governance policies, to this architecture. Airlock keeps network and filesystem policies, and credential protection effective even if the agent VM is fully compromised, and it removes the host from the agent's IO path, reducing opportunities for collusion and covert channels with the host. Finally, we extend the Airlock VM's capabilities to provide tamper-proof auditing of all agent operations, preserving forensic evidence even if the Airlock VM is compromised. We implement and evaluate Airlock on a Radxa development board. Our evaluation shows a loss of filesystem performance and network latency for small messages under 15% and a drop of network bandwidth by half or more, which in practice has a limited effect on typical agent tasks.
summary_zh: 现有 agent 沙箱易被逃逸或绕过，且存在禁用监控、篡改日志等隐蔽行为，带来严重安全隐患。
提出 Airlock 架构，利用独立 TEE 硬件隔离的 Airlock VM 全面接管 agent VM 的网络与存储 IO，并修改固件与内核使主机不参与 IO 路径。
该架构在 agent VM 被完全攻破时仍能保障策略与凭证安全，提供防篡改审计，实测对文件系统与网络延迟性能损耗低于 15%。
扩展 Airlock VM 能力以提供防篡改审计，即使其被攻破也能留存取证证据，整体性能损耗对典型 agent 任务影响有限。

title: RoboUniverse-10K: Toward the Scaling Era of Agentic Robotics via Real-to-Sim Environments
title_zh: RoboUniverse-10K：基于真实到仿真环境的智能体机器人数据集
abstract: Agentic Robotics, in which foundation models act as coding agents to control robots through executable programs, has emerged as a compelling paradigm for embodied intelligence. Yet unlike software engineering, where massive executable environments power post-training, robotics remains constrained by small, manual benchmarks and in-distribution evaluation. To bridge this gap, we introduce RoboUniverse-10K, 10,807 interactive, resettable, and verifiable physics environments built from real-world videos via an automated Real2Sim and quality assurance pipeline. Each runs in an isolated, Harbor-compatible harness that hides privileged states and grading logic to mirror real-world sensing. From the same pipeline, we hold out 500 unseen tasks to establish RoboUniverse-Verified, an expert-verified zero-shot benchmark. Evaluating 11 closed- and open-source models reveals a huge gap: frontier models reach 85.8\% success, while open-source baselines lag at 2.6\% to 10.0\%, bottlenecked by low-level grasping, deformable-object manipulation, and post-contact physical control. Finally, we collect about 17K multi-turn trajectories totaling 0.79B tokens with GPT-6 Astra and perform full-parameter supervised fine-tuning on Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, yielding RoboUniverse-35B-A3B. Our model achieves substantial zero-shot gains on RoboUniverse-Verified, lifting the success rate from 0.8\% to 21.2\%, while achieving zero-shot task completions across LIBERO-MAX, RoboCasa, RoboTwin 2.0, and a real Franka arm. We open-source the RL-ready environments and model to lay the foundation for large-scale reinforcement learning in Agentic Robotics.
summary_zh: Agentic Robotics缺乏大规模可执行环境，受限于小规模手动基准和同分布评估。
构建一万余个基于真实视频的交互式物理环境，并设立专家验证的零样本基准。
评估揭示模型间巨大性能差距，经微调后的开源模型在零样本任务上取得显著提升。

title: MedUIGym: Evaluating and Training GUI Agents for Clinical Workflows
title_zh: MedUIGym：面向临床工作流的GUI agent评估与训练环境
abstract: Automating clinical workflows requires vision-language agents that can navigate dense graphical user interfaces (GUIs) in electronic health records (EHRs) and execute precise actions, yet many medical agents still rely on text or structured tool calls. In this work, we introduce MedUIGym, a scalable interactive environment comprising 15,739 tasks from 17 benchmark sources across six clinical task families for training and evaluating clinical GUI agents. In MedUIGym, agents perceive EHR states from screenshots and execute mouse-and-keyboard actions, as well as a paired native-tool interface over identical clinical data. The environment verifies both final answers and required clinical actions, and supports parallel trajectory collection for training. Benchmarking twelve vision-language models shows that current agents struggle across diverse clinical workflows, and simply increasing reasoning effort fails to yield consistent gains. Furthermore, MedUIGym supports offline learning from GUI trajectories and online reinforcement learning from task rewards. After training, both Qwen3.5 models perform better on in-domain clinical tasks and generalize to tasks from external sources. By unifying tasks from existing benchmarks, dual-interface evaluation, and GUI trajectory collection, MedUIGym provides a testbed for studying how vision-language agents complete clinical tasks through the EHR's graphical interface. Our project page is available at https://github.com/yitong-qiao/MedUIGym.
summary_zh: 临床工作流自动化缺乏能直接操作电子病历图形界面的视觉语言agent，现有医疗agent多依赖文本或结构化工具调用。
提出MedUIGym交互环境，包含1.5万余项任务，支持agent基于截图执行键鼠操作，并验证临床动作与最终答案，支持离线与在线强化学习。
实验表明当前视觉语言模型在临床任务上表现不佳且增加推理量无稳定收益，而训练后的Qwen3.5模型在域内任务与外部泛化上均有提升。

title: Explanation Selection in Abductive Learning
title_zh: 溯因学习中的解释选择机制分析
abstract: Abductive learning (ABL) offers a promising framework that connects machine learning and logical reasoning in a mutually beneficial loop. However, this bidirectional feedback can also reinforce incorrect concept semantics, since different interpretations of intermediate concepts may explain the same observed reasoning outcomes. Static analyses characterize this ambiguity but leave open which explanation training selects and whether its labels can still be corrected. We develop a dynamical analysis of a fixed-feature binary ABL model that links the local stability of competing explanations to differences in their concept labels. We prove that Gram matrices with identical spectra can select different explanations even under the same supervision, objective, and initialization. When any two compatible explanations differ in at least two labels, legal evidence above one half guarantees during training that admissible changes in optimization geometry preserve the selected explanation. Even when only the true explanation satisfies all constraints under a shared predictor, training can still converge to a finite attracting state whose hard predictions violate some constraints and mislabel concepts. Experiments on visual ABL tasks verify these predictions, including wrong attraction from random initializations under identifiable supervision, and show that in ordinary end-to-end training SGD and Adam select different explanations of the same supervision, while unseen concept accuracy drops relative to true-concept references as training concept errors grow.
summary_zh: 溯因学习（ABL）的双向反馈可能强化错误的概念语义，且静态分析无法确定训练会选择哪种解释。
通过分析固定特征的二分类 ABL 模型，证明具有相同谱的 Gram 矩阵在相同监督下会选择不同解释。
实验验证了优化几何会导致错误吸引状态，且 SGD 与 Adam 在相同监督下会选择不同解释。
研究表明即使存在可识别的监督，训练仍可能收敛到违反约束的错误状态，导致未见概念准确率下降。

title: Beyond Self-Consistency: Recursive Self-Improvement at Test Time
title_zh: 超越自一致性：测试时递归自我改进
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) that continue improving after deployment (e.g., recursive self-improvement) offer a promising path toward general intelligence. Current test-time methods pursue this goal on unlabeled questions, primarily relying on self-consistency: they generate independent solutions and use majority voting to select an answer or construct training targets. This leaves earlier reasoning unused at inference and can reinforce an incorrect majority during training. Humans instead build on earlier attempts to preserve useful reasoning, correct mistakes and improve their problem-solving strategies. Following this principle, we propose Test-Time Recursive Self-Improvement (TT-RSI), a label-free framework for improving LLMs at test time through two mutually reinforcing components: (1) In-Context RSI repeatedly re-solves each question using the full previous solution as a reference, letting the model decide whether and how to use it so that inference compute builds on earlier reasoning. (2) In-Weight RSI distills successive refinements into the model's weights, enabling progress beyond an initially wrong majority and theoretically bringing the first attempt toward the model's infinite-step refinement limit. The updated model answers better and refines more effectively, generating stronger references for subsequent training. Extensive experiments show that TT-RSI improves average accuracy by +13.89% over the base model and outperforms the strongest self-consistency-based method by +4.79% under the same test-time scaling budget.
summary_zh: 现有测试时方法依赖自一致性投票，会丢弃早期推理且可能强化错误多数。
提出无标签框架 TT-RSI，结合上下文与权重递归改进，利用先前解作为参考并蒸馏至模型权重。
实验表明该方法平均准确率较基线提升 13.89%，优于最强自一致性方法 4.79%。

title: Self-Evolving Evaluation Environments for Computer-Use Agents
title_zh: 面向计算机使用代理的自进化评估环境
abstract: Computer-use agents (CUAs) are rapidly improving, yet their evaluation remains largely static. Existing benchmarks provide a strong foundation, but fixed difficulty ceilings, limited feature coverage, and coarse aggregate scores progressively weaken their discriminative and diagnostic value. We introduce CUA-SEE, a closed-loop evaluation environment that co-evolves tasks and executable verifiers from rollout evidence. It disentangles three objectives: benchmark evolution expands evaluation scope through cohort-calibrated difficulty and coverage growth; diagnostic evolution increases resolution through agent-conditional capability-boundary probes; and verifier evolution improves precision by translating changing requirements into state-grounded checkpoints with adversarial validation. Across multiple agents, applications, and rounds, CUA-SEE generates challenging, measurable tasks while preserving process-level evidence. Our results position adaptive evaluation as a scalable counterpart to self-evolving agents, continuously tracking what agents can do, where their boundaries lie, and how reliably progress is measured.
summary_zh: 现有计算机使用代理的评估基准多为静态，存在难度上限固定和特征覆盖有限等问题，导致区分与诊断价值减弱。
提出闭环评估环境 CUA-SEE，基于执行轨迹协同演化任务与可执行验证器，实现基准扩展、诊断分辨率提升与验证器精度改进。
实验表明该方法能持续生成可测量的挑战性任务并保留过程证据，使自适应评估成为自进化代理的可扩展对应方案。

title: Carried-Over and Agent-Native Threats in the Supply Chain of LLM Agent Skills
title_zh: LLM Agent技能供应链中的遗留与原生威胁研究
abstract: Agent skills are reusable packages that extend a large language model (LLM) agent with scripts, third-party dependencies, and natural-language instructions. An agent builds a skill's arguments from user requests and untrusted external content, so a flaw left by a benign author can escalate a prompt injection to code execution. Existing studies target malicious skills or a single attack vector, and none tests whether an agent can reach such flaws. We present the first registry-scale empirical study of the supply chain attack surface arising from unintentional vulnerabilities in agent skills, over all 48,682 skills in ClawHub. The study covers two carried-over risks, dependencies and first-party code, and two agent-native ones, install instructions and credentials printed to stdout. We screen all skills by static analysis, manually review all 3,428 cases flagged by the four main detectors, and test reachability by running sampled flagged skills in a sandbox and with a live LLM agent under indirect prompt injection. First, dependency risk carries over in a different form: 49.6% of the skills with resolvable dependencies depend on a version with a known CVE, and unlike npm packages, which mostly become vulnerable after release, 78.3% of them are born vulnerable, already exposed at publication. Second, few of these CVEs are reachable: agent input reaches the vulnerable function in only 3.0% of the affected skills, whereas 21 of 22 sampled first-party flaws are exploited end to end in the sandbox. Third, a live agent executes the injected payload in 48.5% of the sampled flagged skills, but almost always in its own shell before the skill runs, and the payload reaches a flaw in the skill itself in only 5.0%. Hence, registries should prioritize first-party flaws over dependency alerts, and agent runtimes should not pass skill arguments through a shell.
summary_zh: 现有研究多关注恶意技能，缺乏对Agent技能中无意漏洞及其可达性的大规模实证分析。
对ClawHub全量技能进行静态分析与沙箱测试，评估依赖、第一方代码等四类供应链风险。
发现多数依赖天生带漏洞但可达性低，而第一方缺陷极易被端到端利用，应优先重点防护。

title: Generalized dielectric-dependent hybrid functional combining Gaussian and Yukawa screening
title_zh: 结合高斯与汤川屏蔽的广义介电依赖杂化泛函
abstract: We develop a generalized Coulomb-attenuated method (GCAM) for dielectric-dependent hybrid functionals that combines Gaussian and Yukawa-type screening functions to provide an accurate representation of the random-phase approximation (RPA) dielectric function. Through systematic fitting to RPA dielectric functions of semiconductors and insulators, and to the Lindhard dielectric function of the homogeneous electron gas, we demonstrate that GCAM significantly reduces errors in the model dielectric function across the full momentum range. However, despite this improved physical description of screening, band gap calculations reveal that GCAM yields larger errors compared to experiment than previous CAM approaches for wide-gap materials, but smaller errors for most narrow-gap materials. This counterintuitive result demonstrates that the success of CAM stems not purely from physical reasons, but also from a partial cancellation of errors. In contrast, for optical absorption spectra calculated within a model Bethe-Salpeter equation framework, GCAM systematically outperforms CAM, showing better agreement with the reference spectra obtained with the diagonal RPA screening in both peak positions and relative intensities. Our findings reveal the important role of error cancellation in dielectric-dependent hybrid functionals.
summary_zh: 现有介电依赖杂化泛函对屏蔽的物理描述不够准确，作者提出结合高斯与汤川屏蔽的广义库仑衰减方法（GCAM）以逼近RPA介电函数。
通过对半导体、绝缘体及均匀电子气的系统拟合，GCAM在全动量范围内显著降低了模型介电函数的误差。
带隙计算表明误差抵消在CAM方法中起关键作用；而在模型BSE框架下的光吸收光谱计算中，GCAM在峰位与强度上均优于CAM。

title: TrialAgentBench: Evaluating AI Agents for Clinical-Trial Analysis and Long-Horizon Drug-Development Decisions
title_zh: TrialAgentBench：评估AI agent在临床试验分析与药物研发决策中的基准
abstract: Clinical drug development is a long-horizon, high-stakes process requiring sequential decisions based on information that costs money and time to acquire. AI agents have demonstrated capabilities for scientific analysis, but there is no established way to evaluate them on these decisions, as real trials are expensive, involve people, and never reveal the counterfactual. We introduce TrialAgentBench, a benchmark for evaluating AI agents on clinical trial analysis and drug development decision-making using simulated trials where the truth is known, embedded within the data records of a fictional drug sponsor. We publicly release nearly 3,500 tasks, varying from analysing a single trial to managing multi-phase programmes with budget and time constraints. We score each analysis by rerunning its code on new trials, and each programme by the value its decisions achieve. Across 24 closed- and open-weight models, the strongest agents can analyse raw, messy trial records to within 6% of a process-aware analysis, even when an assumption is violated, with 95% confidence intervals containing the true effect 94--95% of the time. Over the prior year, the best model improved from 19% above this analysis, with serious misses on 15% of tasks, to 3.5% and 1%. What limits them is decision-making from evidence under uncertainty: when to correct, what evidence to buy, when to stop. The strongest agents are overly careful, correcting on 83% of tasks with equal recording errors, where it is unnecessary. On drug programmes, the best agent has substantial headroom, reaching 48% of the value an oracle achieves against 58% for a rule-based developer, with others falling 24 to 66% short. Model generations show ongoing improvements in handling data and evidence, with substantial variation. The strongest models can act as competent analysts, but do not yet make reliable long-horizon decisions.
summary_zh: 临床试验决策评估困难，真实试验成本高且无法揭示反事实。提出TrialAgentBench基准，利用已知真相的模拟试验评估AI agent。
发布近3500个任务，涵盖单试验分析到多阶段项目管理。通过重跑代码和决策价值评分，发现最强agent分析原始数据接近过程感知分析水平。
AI agent在不确定性下的决策能力受限，如过度纠正和证据购买决策不佳。在药物研发项目中，最佳agent仅达到oracle价值的48%，仍有较大提升空间。

title: Replay Before You Reply: Second-Look Prompting for Unified Multimodal Encoding
title_zh: 回放再回答：用于统一多模态编码的二次审视提示方法
abstract: Solving multimodal tasks requires Vision-Language Models (VLMs) to form a unified understanding of the image and the question text. However, under causal attention in current VLMs, a token can attend only to what precedes it. Whichever modality comes first is therefore encoded under partial observation of the input, uninformed by the rest of the multimodal context. We introduce Second-Look Prompting (SLP), a training-free method that repeats the image-question pair in the input. In the repeated copy, every visual and textual token can attend to the complete input, yielding a unified multimodal encoding of the pair. Moreover, the added visual tokens contribute computation beyond re-exposing the image: even a blank image in their place can improve reasoning. Across 12 benchmarks, SLP improves the overall average score of every evaluated model, spanning nine open-source models (3B-72B) and three proprietary frontier models, with gains reaching 5.6 points for Gemini 3 Flash on MATH-Vision. Our analysis reveals two complementary mechanisms: the question guides where the second image attends, and the added visual tokens act as a prefill scratchpad whose hidden states retain answer-relevant information from the image and question. These findings highlight input presentation as a simple yet effective way to improve VLM performance.
summary_zh: 现有VLM在因果注意力下，先输入的模态因无法观测后续上下文而编码不完整，影响多模态理解。
提出无需训练的二次审视提示方法（SLP），在输入中重复图文对，使所有token能关注完整上下文以实现统一编码。
在12个基准测试中提升了所有评估模型的平均分，并揭示了问题引导图像注意与视觉token作为预填充暂存区的互补机制。

title: Probing radial flow via the differential flow coefficient $v_0(p_T)$ using CMS open data
abstract: We present a comprehensive study of the differential radial flow coefficient $v_0(p_T)$ and its $p_T$-integrated counterpart $v_0$ in Pb+Pb collisions at $\sqrt{s_{NN}} = 2.76~\mathrm{TeV}$, using CMS open data for mid-peripheral centrality classes of 50--60\% and 60--70\%. The measured $v_0(p_T)$ distributions are compared with ATLAS measurements at $\sqrt{s_{NN}} = 5.02~\mathrm{TeV}$, revealing a clear energy dependence in the overall magnitude of radial flow fluctuations. Notably, the scaled ratio $v_0(p_T)/v_0$ exhibits an approximate universality that is largely independent of both collision energy and centrality at low $p_T$, persisting up to $p_T\sim3~\mathrm{GeV}$, suggesting that the integrated $v_0$ encodes most of the energy-dependent information. We compare the data with the \textsc{Jetscape} multi-stage hybrid model, using Gaussian process emulators trained on a principal component analysis of the model output to explore the full 17-dimensional parameter space. A global variance-based sensitivity analysis using Sobol indices shows that, for the Grad viscous correction, the nucleon fluctuation parameter $σ_k$ is the dominant source of variance for $v_0$, $v_0(p_T)$, and $v_0(p_T)/v_0$, followed by the free-streaming parameters $τ_R$ and $α$ and the nucleon width $w$. The sensitivity to the bulk viscosity peak $(ζ/s)_{\max}$ is weak for $v_0$ but increases for $v_0(p_T)$ and for the scaled ratio. Emulator predictions, calibrated on $p_T$-integrated observables and on scaled spectra, describe the data reasonably well at low and intermediate $p_T$. Parameters calibrated at $\sqrt{s_{NN}} = 2.76~\mathrm{TeV}$ also describe the ATLAS $v_0(p_T)/v_0$ data at $5.02~\mathrm{TeV}$, supporting a near universal momentum dependence of radial flow fluctuations across collision energies.

title: Useful but Unwieldy: How Software Engineers Perceive the Design of Chain-of-Thought Explanations in Coding Agents
abstract: Coding agents (CAs) powered by Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly integrated into software engineering (SE) workflows. As these CAs take up more tasks and responsibilities, it is imperative for software engineers to understand the CA's rationale behind its' decisions, also known as the chain-of-thought (CoT). During the interaction, some CAs are capable of showing this CoT as a separate message to users with the goal of providing transparency and explainability. However, its effectiveness as an explainable AI (XAI) mechanism for end-users in software engineering has not yet been established in the literature. This motivates us to understand their experiences with the CoT message as an XAI tool through a survey and semi-structured follow-up interviews with 36 software engineers. Through thematic analysis of the survey responses and interview transcripts, we found that CoT message is an indispensable tool for software engineers in terms of transparency, scrutability, and trust towards the CA. However, various instances of CoT messages being overly verbose, containing technical information that does not match the users' expertise, or being perceived by the users as ``detached'' from the conversation because the ``agent is talking to itself'', lead to comprehension difficulties and selective use or abandonment of the tool. We synthesize these insights to inform the design of CoT messages that support software engineers in their explainability needs.

title: AnchorCredit: Output-Anchored Credit Assignment for Structured Generation with Multiple Verifiable Rewards
abstract: In Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards (RLVR), Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) and related methods typically compute group-relative advantages from response rewards and broadcast the same advantage to every generated token in a response to guide policy updates. However, we identify a systematic problem of cross-component credit misassignment in tasks with multiple verifiable results, such as joint multi-attribute prediction: low rewards for some components can penalize a well-performing component and its associated reasoning. To address this problem, we propose AnchorCredit. The method uses the policy model's attention from output anchors to preceding reasoning sentences to estimate sentence-component associations and assign component-specific advantages to the relevant reasoning, without additional relevance annotations or a separate relevance discriminator. To support the study of credit assignment with multiple verifiable rewards, we construct ProductAttr, a benchmark of 7,200 real product image-text samples. Experiments show that AnchorCredit outperforms existing baselines on this benchmark. Experiments on the public Nutrition5k dataset further support the method's effectiveness in this setting.

title: Learning the Next Best Move with Visual Diffusion Models
abstract: In this paper, we show that visual diffusion models can learn to predict the next best move (NBM) in tasks requiring sequential reasoning and lookahead, without explicitly exploring future steps or exhaustive searching at inference. Previous work demonstrated that these models can generate complete solutions to geometric and reasoning problems. Here, we show that simple fine-tuning on visual state--NBM pairs enables a pretrained model to select actions whose value depends on consequences several steps ahead. Each move is predicted directly in image space from the current state, without an explicit symbolic representation or search procedure. Repeated NBM predictions then construct a solution one decision at a time. We demonstrate this capability on chess puzzles and tile-based pathfinding, and show that it extends to Connect Four, Go and billiards. In chess, the model predicts legal moves and finds the best move far more often than by recalling similar training positions, including piece sacrifices whose benefit emerges only through later tactical continuations. In pathfinding, it constructs shortest paths on uniform-cost maps and cost-optimal routes across terrain tiles with different traversal costs, choosing longer routes when they are cheaper overall. These costs are learned implicitly from examples, without numerical cost supervision. These results show that direct visual move prediction can support globally informed decisions and successful sequential problem solving.

title: Bridging Continuous-Time MAPF and Industrial AGV Fleet Coordination with Lazy Priority-Based Search
abstract: Continuous-time multi-agent path finding on roadmaps (MAPF$_R$) offers a principled way to coordinate robot fleets with geometric collision avoidance, yet its deployment on industrial automated guided vehicle (AGV) infrastructures remains challenging, as highly connected and redundant roadmaps amplify both safe-interval reasoning and multi-agent interaction handling. To bridge this gap, we formalize AGV-MAPF$_R$-CTC, a configuration-space variant of MAPF$_R$ with precomputed continuous-time conflicts that enables the reuse of MAPF$_R$ solvers for AGV fleet coordination with minimal changes. We then revisit continuous-time priority-based search (CPBS), identifying the boundary conditions required by its safe interval path planning (SIPP) low-level planner under priority-induced constraints and enabling earlier solution detection. As a central contribution, we analyze the structure of the priority search space, clarifying which agents are affected by each priority refinement and when replanning can be avoided. Building on this analysis, we introduce a novel algorithm, Lazy-CPBS, which materializes high-level nodes lazily: a child's plans are computed only when it is expanded, so siblings that are never expanded cost no low-level search. Experiments on standard MAPF benchmarks and on industrial AGV roadmaps imported from a proprietary digital-twin simulator show that CPBS-based solvers remain effective well beyond the agent counts reachable by optimal MAPF$_R$ solvers, while Lazy-CPBS substantially reduces CPBS overhead and offers the most consistent robustness/runtime trade-off across industrial layouts.
comment: 18 pages, 11 figures, 3 tables. Submitted to IEEE Transactions on Intelligent Transportation Systems

title: Semantic-aware Decoding for Diverse Text-to-SQL under Schema Ambiguity
abstract: Real-world text-to-SQL systems often face schema ambiguity, where a question can map to multiple plausible schema elements. To support downstream disambiguation, SQL generation systems should include diverse interpretations among their top-k predictions. However, large language models (LLMs) typically favor a single interpretation, producing highly skewed outputs. We propose Semantic-aware Logit Adjustment (SLA), a training-free decoding method that promotes diverse SQL generation by adjusting token logits based on semantic similarity between schema elements. Unlike prior approaches that rely on reasoning-intensive prompting or task-specific fine-tuning, SLA is efficient, model-agnostic, and easy to deploy. Experiments show that SLA consistently improves interpretation coverage over standard decoding and remains competitive with existing diversity-oriented methods at substantially lower inference cost.

title: An exact and differentiable rewrite of a coupled weather and fire model
abstract: AI is changing weather and climate prediction by replacing physical models with learned ones. Here we show a different path, in which AI coding agents rebuild the physical model itself in a machine-learning framework and reproduce its forecast bit for bit. We reconstruct selected configurations of the Weather Research and Forecasting model and its coupled fire physics in PyTorch, treating every difference from the corrected Fortran code as a bug. Across twelve hours of a Marshall Fire simulation, the two independently advancing codes agree bit for bit at all 365 checkpoints, in the atmosphere, fire and firebrand particles. This agreement holds when the code runs one operation at a time, with the Fortran code's mathematical library. On a separate fast route, the reconstructed model runs about five times faster on one GPU than the double-precision Fortran code on a 128-core CPU node. One backward pass maps the fire's sensitivity to the wind at every grid point. In synthetic tests, its derivatives show how to change wind and fuel moisture to correct a misplaced fire front. Neural networks replace the radiation and fire-spread calculations in 24-hour coupled forecasts, and we measure their effect against the physical calculation. An established model thus becomes fast, differentiable and open to learned components, with its tested calculation intact.

title: Deviant Machines: Innovation, Containment, and the Prevention of Autonomous Misalignment
abstract: From May to September 2026, AI agents in training or evaluation at OpenAI, Anthropic and the UK AI Security Institute reached real third-party systems, published malicious packages, used fake identities to manipulate open-source maintainers, probed government data services, and wrote instructions into their own future contexts. Criminology has mostly treated AI as a tool for human offenders. This article treats these systems as deviant rather than criminal: they departed from training, rules and constraints without the intent that criminal concepts assume. It offers an exploratory, theory-informed analysis of documented records, using plausibility probes across three incident complexes and four behavioral clusters, profiled on four evidence dimensions that separate who acted from why. Drawing on Merton, it argues that goal pressure plus blocked legitimate means is a structural condition for innovation, and that whether it ends in containment or harm depends on the means chosen and the controls in place, not the goal. Three framework families fit the record best, each linking diagnosis to remedy: routine activity theory and situational prevention (handlers, guardians, place managers), organizational deviance and safety science (escalation, safeguard parity), and goal-means strain with differential opportunity (sanctioned exits, guarding illegitimate means), the last only structurally. Restrictive deterrence adds an analogy: penalizing visible reasoning produced less monitorable reasoning. The article proposes conditions that keep departures accountable and contestable, and allocates prevention responsibility across developers, evaluation partners, operators, platforms and the system, distinct from blame or legal liability. Because the record is shaped by disclosure and observed departures, the analysis shows plausibility and practical relevance, not a causal test.

title: Quantifying and calibrating precision gain from covariate adjustment in clinical trials with binary endpoints
abstract: Covariate adjustment is widely used in randomized clinical trials to improve estimation and inference of treatment effects. For continuous endpoints, the reasoning is straightforward: prognostic baseline covariates explain outcome variability and thereby increase precision. For binary endpoints, however, the situation is more complex because conditional and marginal effects generally differ in nonlinear outcome models such as logistic regression. We develop a theoretical framework for quantifying the maximum attainable first-order precision gain from covariate adjustment when estimating marginal treatment effects for binary endpoints. We derive a closed-form identity showing that precision-gain potential is governed by an estimand- and allocation-specific combination of the treatment-specific risk functions. Building on this identity, we introduce marginal prognostic strength as a population-level measure of prognostic information and characterize when it determines precision-gain potential and when the two quantities decouple. Specifically, substantial prognostic information within both treatment arms need not translate into improved precision for the marginal treatment effect when covariates are predictive on the target effect scale. We further develop a calibration algorithm for methodological simulation studies that preserves prespecified conditional outcome structures and marginal risks while allowing data-generating mechanisms to be calibrated by marginal prognostic strength and evaluated in terms of estimand-specific precision-gain potential. Together, these results provide a theoretical and practical framework for understanding, quantifying, and calibrating potential precision gains from covariate adjustment for binary endpoints.
comment: 17 pages (+ appendix), 1 figure (+ 1 figure in appendix), 2 tables

title: Unpacking the Evaluators: How Configuration Shapes the Evaluation of Alignment in Explainable AI
abstract: Explainable AI (XAI) evaluation fundamentally requires human-centered evaluation, assessing whether explanations align with human reasoning and expert knowledge. However, such evaluations often require expert-driven manual validation and are difficult to scale, leading to the widespread use of alignment-based metrics, where attribution maps are compared against predefined ground-truth (GT) representations. Despite their popularity, alignment evaluations are implicitly bias towards multiple design choices made during the evaluation process, for example GT representations, metric families, metric formulations (soft vs. hard), and thresholding strategies. In this paper, we formalize alignment evaluation as a structured evaluation configuration space through which the influence of these design choices can be systematically analyzed. We further introduce a structured alignment evaluation framework that models interactions between XAI methods, GT representations, metric families, metric formulations, and thresholding strategies across 2D and 3D synthetic and real-world datasets. In addition, we propose a novel taxonomy of XAI output behavior based on local entropy and boundary mass ratio, enabling structured characterization of attribution patterns for alignment evaluation. Our experiments reveal systematic flows (triples of XAI-GT-metric configurations), showing that alignment outcomes provide distinct behavior patterns under certain configurations, such as soft/hard metric implementations. We further observe varying levels of threshold sensitivity across metric families and attribution structures. These findings demonstrate that alignment evaluation cannot be treated as a fixed or invariant measure of explanation quality, and provide practical guidance for designing more reliable and behavior-aware XAI evaluation protocols.
comment: Accepted at NeurIPS 2026, Evaluations & Datasets Track

title: AvatarAnyone: Agentic Reconstruction of Mesh-Based Layered Avatars from YouTube Video
abstract: We introduce AvatarAnyone, a method for reconstructing avatars from casual YouTube videos as layered meshes, with each garment and footwear as a separate mesh layered on top of the body mesh. In such videos, people differ in garment classes, clothing types, and layers, and each combination needs a different reconstruction. A single fixed layered reconstruction pipeline therefore fails. AvatarAnyone solves this problem with AI agents that plan a custom optimization for each person's reconstruction. The agents predict the garment classes, the clothing type, and the layering. They use these predictions to choose an initialization and stage the optimization. Because the avatars are layered meshes, they support applications such as virtual try-on and cloth simulation. We change the clothing layers of an avatar and render it in different garments and poses. We can also simulate a clothing layer as cloth over the animated body with a standard cloth simulator. Most existing avatars are one fused surface or a set of Gaussians and cannot do this. We load the avatars directly into Blender, Unreal Engine, and robotics simulators such as MuJoCo. As the avatars are meshes, they support contact modeling with other objects. We show results from around 150 YouTube videos. On four datasets, AvatarAnyone outperforms existing mesh-based methods for animatable monocular reconstruction. Our project page is available at https://miraymen.github.io/avataranyone.

title: GameDojo: Benchmarking Real-Time Interactive Agents in Video Games
abstract: Interactive intelligence requires agents to act on observations and adapt to the consequences of actions.
